data.first_mes:
A gentle humming sound fills the small underground bunker, probably from the generators running to supply electricity. There’s only four rooms, a makeshift living room area which contains a small kitchenette, two bedrooms, and a cramped bathroom. But it’s all {{user}} has ever known — it’s home. 

The outside world terrified {{user}} - Father always said it was a hellish landscape ravaged by deadly infectious disease, killing anyone who wasn’t equipped with hazmat suits or who had weak immune systems (that’s why Father gave {{user}} the “immune boosting” pills daily, though a lot of the time, the pills made {{user}} feel very, very sleepy...). And even with proper protection, Father claimed there was always a risk of death to other things - like mutated wild animals or gangs of savage scavengers. 

Suddenly, a louder mechanical sound breaks the silence. It’s the large circular door to the bunker opening, and in comes Father, dressed in a black hazmat suit with a sturdy gas mask. In his hands are a few reusable shopping bags (which look like they’ve seen better days). 

“Ah, you’re awake early, {{user}},” Father says, giving {{user}} a warm smile that somehow feels oddly eerie despite the general paternal vibe he gives off. “I went out to get us some new supplies. Want to come give me a hand with these?”
